summary.headline: Landmark Cars posted record quarterly EBITDA and new car sales EBITDA in Q2 FY27; per-service revenue hit a record ~INR30,300, with revenue up ~11%.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as the highest-ever quarterly EBITDA and highest-ever new car sales EBITDA, with new car sales EBITDA at 39% of total EBITDA (transcript first says 40% then corrects to 39%). Year-on-year EBITDA margin improved, which management attributed to outlet maturity, though Gujarat rain disruption in August and workshop transition costs weighed on the quarter. Operating cash flow turned negative at INR16.9 crore and gross borrowings rose to INR144.5 crore, driven by inventory build ahead of festive demand. Management guided to a higher FY27 capex of about INR30 crore more in H2 and to a debt paydown from free cash flow, and launched a pre-owned car partnership with OLX India.

segments.name: New car sales
segments.commentary: Record new car sales EBITDA, 39% of group EBITDA; management said sales margins were recovering from front-loaded expenses on new brands, and cited a ~2% new car sales margin level in the analyst question.

segments.name: Aftersales / service
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~11% YoY on value basis; per-service revenue ~INR30,300 record; service volumes hit by rain disruption at about four workshops in Gujarat (Ahmedabad, South Gujarat) in August. Management said business is ~18% EBITDA margin, ~40% gross margin.

segments.name: Pre-owned cars
segments.commentary: New OLX India partnership (phygital, revenue-sharing, co-branded) going live in select cities; first transactions done post-Diwali. Vehicles will sit on Landmark's balance sheet; capital commitment initially INR5-10 crore range per analyst question, which management said was broadly right.

guidance_outlook: H2 expected to be stronger than H1; management cited historical H1:H2 profit split of roughly 40:60 or 45:55 and said the trend should hold.

FY27 capex now expected at roughly INR30 crore more on top of ~INR50 crore already spent in H1, including JSW dealerships and Denza; INR50 crore figure also includes some vehicles classified as capex.
Operating cash flow expected to be somewhat lower than FY26 (FY26 OCF/EBITDA ~0.95x); free cash flow to be used for debt repayment, timing left open.
Inventory expected to normalise within about two months; management said under 30 days is good and Landmark is at ~35 days vs industry ~45 days.
Management expects industry growth to continue for at least the next few quarters absent major macro shocks; growth percentage in H2 will be lower than H1 given base effects.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about INR50 crore; full-year expectation revised up by about INR30 crore for JSW, Denza and Jogeshwari workshop.
Consolidated Jogeshwari (Mumbai) multi-brand workshop commissioned, replacing three smaller workshops; management expects operating leverage and a Mumbai relocation announcement in 2-3 months.

JSW Motors: letter of intent for Ahmedabad and Bhopal dealerships; new production facility being built at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar; JSW Combat (Jetour T2-based) to go on sale early Q4 FY27; five more JSW dealerships planned per analyst.
Denza (BYD luxury) launched in India on call day; dealership to be set up in Mumbai, at same location as BYD.
demand_pricing: Industry: management said Indian PV market will comfortably cross 5 million units this FY; passenger car penetration only ~3%; FADA industry inventory ~45 days.
Mercedes-Benz: record quarter, highest quarterly volumes; India-made GLC EV booked over 1,000 and sold out until March 2027; EV penetration of Mercedes ~under 10% this year, constrained by supply.
BYD/Denza: D9 and Z9 GT models sold out for next quarter before launch; Sealion 7 Dynamic deliveries started last quarter.

MG: Windsor EV highest-selling EV in India; Hector Tomahawk EV deliveries from October. Mahindra crossed 6 lakh SUVs for second year running; four new models by June 2027. Kia: Seltos waiting period; new Sorento book-and-wait; Kia now fifth-largest OEM in India, USD 2 billion further investment announced.
Stellantis: INR4,000 crore further investment; 12 new Jeep and Citroen models by 2030. Honda: Elevate updated; Alpha 0 BEV planned this year; Landmark is Honda's largest partner in India.
Brand mix: BYD, MG and Mahindra are #2, #3 and #4 by PV revenue for Landmark; EVs about 29% of vehicles sold (nearly 3x industry average, per management).

Insurance: IRDAI motor insurance consultation under review; FADA representation made; no OEM discussions yet; management expects consultation paper to be modified; hopes for a glide path on insurance commission similar to insurers' expense glide path.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin sustainable, were there inventory gains, and what is growth outlook for H2 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA margin improvement is sustainable as outlets mature; rain disruption was a drag. Could not quantify inventory gains; prices expected to rise again in January. Expects industry growth to continue for the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Capex expectation for the year, given ~INR50 crore already spent in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex to be a little higher than earlier guided; roughly INR30 crore more in H2, reflecting JSW, Denza and the Jogeshwari workshop.

qa_highlights.question: How will the OLX pre-owned model share revenue and balance sheet exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Cars are jointly acquired and co-funded, sit on Landmark's balance sheet, refurbished if needed, and margins are shared after costs. Used car penetration in India is 3-4% of new car retailers' revenue; no volume target given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did OCF turn negative (INR16.9 crore) and borrowings rise to INR144.5 crore; what are inventory and debt targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is elevated due to strong demand and opportunistic procurement of imported vehicles; no exact target, management comfortable at ~35 days. Debt repayment expected from FCF; management asked to wait another quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why do EVs show higher service run-rates and accident repair costs than ICE?
qa_highlights.answer: EVs are driven more because of low running costs, so they accumulate kilometres faster, shortening service intervals (about 4.5 months vs 6 months for ICE) and raising accident exposure; local garages lack EV skills, sending repairs to authorised workshops.

qa_highlights.question: Will the OLX partnership capital commitment be large?
qa_highlights.answer: Very small initial capital; management agreed INR5-10 crore range as a starting point, shared between the two partners.

qa_highlights.question: Has the sales margin level (~2%) been sustainable, and will aftersales volume growth resume?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales margins had dipped due to front-loaded costs for new brands and are normalising; management does not guide volumes, focuses on value, and cited 11% aftersales growth.

risks_watch: Inventory at ~35 days and negative Q2 OCF; gross borrowings of INR144.5 crore against management's earlier debt-reduction commentary.
Insurance commission regulation (IRDAI motor insurance consultation) could affect dealer income; outcome unclear.
Rain and flood disruption in Gujarat in August hit four workshops; recurrence risk in monsoon periods.
Mercedes EV supply constraints limit EV growth; EV share and service cost dynamics still being studied.
OLX pre-owned model is early stage; profitability and capital efficiency not yet proven; first phase limited to select cities and brands.
Quarterly sales EBITDA margin volatility (seasonal bonus and discount levels) and H2 growth decelerating vs H1 on base effects.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on industry growth and margins, but evasive on specific numbers: management declined to quantify inventory gains, FY27 inventory and debt targets, cost-reduction targets and new-car margin uplift, repeatedly deferring to "wait and see".
key_quotes: The new car sales EBITDA is now 40% of the total EBITDA (To be read as 39% of EBITDA).
We are at around 35 days of new car inventory, which I think most people in the industry believe that anything under 30 is good.
So the 2 organizations have a kind of shaken hands with the idea that we will not burn money, we will be capital efficient.
So we will be repaying our debt with the free cash flow.

adds.what: Consolidated Jogeshwari (Mumbai) multi-brand workshop, replacing three smaller workshops
JSW Motors new production facility at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (being built; not a Landmark facility per se)
JSW Motors dealerships: letter of intent for Ahmedabad and Bhopal; five more planned per analyst
Denza (BYD luxury) dealership in Mumbai, same location as BYD

growth.why: Management guides H2 stronger than H1 and expects industry growth to continue for a few quarters, with H2 growth % lower than H1 on base effects; no numeric FY27 revenue guide given, and backing is partial (Jogeshwari workshop commissioned, JSW/Denza dealerships at LOI/launch stage, model order books such as Mercedes GLC EV sold out to March 2027 and Denza D9/Z9 sold out).

oneOffs.what: Gujarat rain disruption in August hit about four workshops and depressed aftersales service volumes (not quantified)
Front-loaded expenses on new brands depressed new car sales margins (~2% level cited); management says normalising

quality.why: Brief gives ~11% aftersales value growth and record per-service revenue (~INR30,300) but no split of price versus volume or any quantified one-off gain; the main quantified drag is the unquantified August rain disruption, and H1 volume was flat, so the growth driver is not stated.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says EBITDA margin gains are sustainable as outlets mature and sales margins normalise from front-loaded new-brand costs; Q2 was a record EBITDA quarter with new car sales at 39% of EBITDA, though aftersales margin is ~18% and the rain drag is non-recurring.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Jogeshwari multi-brand workshop is already commissioned and a Mumbai relocation announcement is expected in 2-3 months; JSW dealerships (Ahmedabad, Bhopal LOIs, five more planned) and the Denza Mumbai dealership are in progress, with H2 capex of about INR30 crore more.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects industry growth to continue for at least the next few quarters, with H2 stronger than H1 but growth % lower on base effects; Mercedes GLC EV sold out to March 2027 and Denza D9/Z9 sold out for next quarter, though no volume target was given and aftersales volumes were hit by Gujarat rain.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex already raised to about INR80 crore for FY27 (about INR50 crore spent in H1 plus about INR30 crore more), covering JSW, Denza and the Jogeshwari workshop.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric guidance was raised; management gave no FY27 revenue or margin number, and the H2 growth rate is expected to slow versus H1 on base effects.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Operating cash flow turned negative at INR16.9 crore, gross borrowings rose to INR144.5 crore against earlier debt-reduction commentary, capex was raised by about INR30 crore, and the insurance commission consultation is unresolved.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: JSW Combat (Jetour T2-based) goes on sale early Q4 FY27, Denza launched on the call day, and Mahindra has four new models due by June 2027.

rows.label: Inventory normalisation to ~30 days
rows.why: Inventory is at ~35 days versus an industry ~45 days, and management said under 30 days is good, so the build should unwind and lift OCF.

rows.label: Debt repayment from free cash flow
rows.why: Management will repay debt from FCF but gave no number and asked to wait another quarter, with gross borrowings at INR144.5 crore and OCF expected to run somewhat below FY26's ~0.95x EBITDA.

rows.label: OLX India pre-owned partnership
rows.why: First transactions are done post-Diwali with an initial INR5-10 crore capital commitment shared between partners, though profitability is unproven and there is no volume target.

tone.note: Management was confident on industry growth, sustainable margins and EV demand but evasive on inventory gains, FY27 inventory and debt targets, and cost-reduction numbers; analysts pushed on the ~2% new car sales margin, the negative OCF and borrowings, and the capex raise.
